problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2u-6v-2,\,y=5v-u+9.
$$

Suppose that $A$ is the matrix that represents the linear transformation associated with $T.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=4$
- The transformation is invertible
worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false. The given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-6v-2 \\ 5v-u+9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-6v \\ -u+5v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}]\ne [\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

- Statement II is true. Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}|=5\cdot 2-(-6)\cdot (-1)=4\ne 0.
$$

- Statement III is true. Since $det(A)\ne 0,$ the affine transformation is invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
